title: Cones of Meaning
lines: Cones of Meaning examines the frames that make some answers seem natural.
The book asks readers to inspect what an explanation includes, excludes, and treats as important.
It connects how people reason with how AI systems select what matters.
A cone is not presented as a literal mechanism inside a mind or model.
Readers gain a way to challenge a frame without abandoning rigorous reasoning.

title: Which frame chose the question
lines: An explanation begins by making some differences relevant and leaving others outside its frame.
A change of purpose can therefore change what a rigorous answer needs to include.
The book asks who selects that frame and who carries the consequences of its omissions.
Moving between frames does not mean that every explanation becomes equally good.
It means making the conditions of reasoning available for examination.

title: When a metaphor overreaches
lines: A cone can help picture selective orientation without explaining a mechanism by itself.
The book distinguishes mathematical resemblance, useful analogy, and evidence for a causal claim.
Its own vocabulary must face that discipline rather than gain protection from it.
Descriptions of AI orientation do not establish that models possess phenomenal consciousness.
These boundaries keep a suggestive framework open to correction instead of turning it into doctrine.

title: Read the frame as well
lines: Begin with the relation between ordinary reasoning and reflection on its chosen premises.
Then follow the examples where relevance changes with purpose, context, or responsibility.
The later cautions test what the book's central metaphor can legitimately support.
Cones of Meaning offers a way to inspect orientation while preserving the demands of reasoning.
Read it to notice when a compelling answer leaves the important question outside its frame.
